title: Applied ML — weekly deep dive: quant + eval onboarding (Aug 31 2026)
content:
Summary:
This doc is the week-in-review for the applied-ml team focusing on quantization experiments, eval onboarding for new open models, and a short triage of KV-cache regressions we saw in canary. High-level takeaways:
- AWQ/GPTQ mixed sweep for rwd-3b-v1 yields ~1.6x median throughput improvement and ~28% token-cost reduction on Dedicated. Quality delta small (0.6% EM drop on our small QA eval set for the best quant profile).
- KV-cache mismatch in the runtime found with q4_hybrid variants: causes occasional state divergence when autoscaling slices are rotated; root cause likely a padding/stride handling difference.
- Onboarding checklist for new open models now includes an explicit quant-profile smoke test and a preflight eval (20 prompts from RedTeam eval set).

Meeting notes (Aug 31 — Sep 2):
Attendees: Priya (owner), Liam, Sofia, Ethan, Marco (SRE), Jenna (console).

Mon 2026-08-31 — deep-dive sync
- Quick status: quant sweep running end-to-end (GPTQ, AWQ, NF4 baselines).
- Liam: finished the GPU memory profiling scripts. Observed peak KV-cache footprint increases by 12% for AWQ q4_hybrid compared to q4_nfq.
- Sofia: eval harness integrated with redwood-evals for automatic metric collection. First run: 10-shot summarization + 5-shot QA. Saved output buckets to s3://redwood-applied-ml/quant-sweeps/2026-08-31/.
- Blocker: autoscaling interactions with shard rebalancer (Marco) — we saw a 5s latency spike during scale-out when q4_hybrid instances were brought online.
- Decision: add a small grace period and KV-cache warmup phase (3s) before routing traffic to newly started shards. Marco owns a follow-up.

Tue 2026-09-01 — lunchtime quick triage
- Observed a single canary failure (trace attached in slack). Reproduction steps (Ethan): run model rwd-3b-v1 q4_hybrid with batched streaming with prefix sizes >1024 tokens. State divergence after step N+3 (old vs new).
- Hypothesis: stride/padding bug in the runtime backend transform for quantized attention keys.
- Action: bisect kernels used by AWQ runtime path; Ethan to run kernel-level unit tests that compare q4_hybrid->float32 reference for KV writes. Target: PR with failing unit test by EOD Wed.

Wed 2026-09-02 — weekly wrap + planning
- Evaluation results (first pass):
  - GPTQ q4 (baseline): throughput +1.3x, EM change -0.9% on QA set, latency P95 +6%
  - AWQ q4_hybrid (best candidate): throughput +1.6x, EM change -0.6%, latency P95 -2% (better due to kernel fusion)
  - NF4 (intended minimal quality loss) : throughput +1.4x, EM change -0.2% but 10% memory overhead vs q4_hybrid
- Cost modeling: for the customer workload sampled (median prompt len 420 tokens, 2.1 tokens/sec generation) we estimate per-token cost reduction of 24–30% depending on batching. Numbers in sheet linked_artifacts.
- Onboarding checklist updated (Sofia): will add 3 automated gates:
  1) RedTeam quick quality gate (20 tokens/20 prompts)
  2) Throughput baseline vs float32 (>=1.2x for q4 variants)
  3) KV-cache regression smoke test (prefix lengths: 0, 512, 1024, 2048)
- Decisions: prioritize AWQ q4_hybrid for next canary but only after KV-cache fix + warmup window.

Action items (owners):
- Ethan: add kernel unit test reproducing KV-cache divergence; open PR and link to JIRA-ML-1298. Due Wed EOD (in progress).
- Marco: implement warmup gating + 3s grace period in rebalancer and autoscaler; add integration test. Due Thu.
- Liam: prepare larger batch sweep (scale up to 8 concurrent requests) to validate throughput at production percentiles. Include cost sheet update. Due next Tue.
- Sofia: wire the new onboarding gates into redwood-evals pipeline and add a dashboard tile in Console for quant-profile health. Due next week.
- Priya: draft rollout playbook for AWQ canary including automatic rollback on quality regression >1% EM (link in linked_artifacts). Due Fri.

Notes from experiments (short log):
- Experiment id: quant-sweep-aug31-run3
- Model: rwd-3b-v1 (float32 baseline)
- Variants tested: gptq-q4, awq-q4_hybrid, nf4-int8
- Hardware: Dedicated G4dn-esque instance (A100-equivalent cluster, 8x per-pod GPU emulation) — note: this cluster uses our staging profile, not exact prod.
- Observed perf: AWQ q4_hybrid had lower end-to-end P95 when streaming enabled — hypothesis: kernel fusion removed an extra kernel launch per generation step.
- Quality checks: small QA set (n=200) showed AWQ EM delta -0.6% (p=.08) vs float32; manual spot-checks show hallucination patterns unchanged. Need larger eval to be confident.

Triage on KV-cache divergence (technical details):
- Reproduction steps (short):
  1) Load rwd-3b-v1 q4_hybrid in canary pool.
  2) Create two parallel requests: one with long prefix (~1200 tokens) then a short continuation stream; the second a fresh request to the same shard after autoscaler triggered scale-out.
  3) Compare token-by-token outputs — divergence occurs on 3rd generation token after warmup for some seeds.
- Suspected cause: an off-by-one when copying padded KV tensors when stride != 1 (happens in quantized kernels that pack in 16-byte blocks).
- Proposed interim mitigation: disallow autoscale immediate routing to newly created q4_hybrid shards until kernel-level fix; add per-request deterministic checksum for KV-copies in debug builds.

Onboarding: new model checklist (short):
- Pull model + conversion sanity (sha check)
- Float32 smoke eval (5 prompts)
- Quant sweep (gptq, awq, nf4) — small sample run
- Quality gate in redwood-evals (20 prompts, RedTeam subset)
- KV-cache smoke (prefix 0..2048)
- Perf baseline (P50/P95 for median workload)
- Console tile + rollback policy defined

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- AWQ q4_hybrid looks good for throughput, but maintenance surface is larger than GPTQ (custom kernels). Is the extra complexity justified for a 20–30% cost reduction? Suggest we gate AWQ behind Dedicated customers with higher throughput SLA first.
- Do we standardize on NF4 for enterprise builds due to quality predictability? NF4 memory overhead might be acceptable for enterprise customers with reserved capacity.

Misc notes / links / scratch: (shorthand)
- quick perf command: ./bench -m rwd-3b-v1 --quant awq-q4_hybrid --batch 4 --streams 8 --prefix 420
- redwood-evals job: run/2026-08-30-quant-sweep (results at s3://.../metrics.json)
- slack logs: thread "quantization-test-aug" for traces
- Jira: JIRA-ML-1298 (kv-cache-divergence), JIRA-ML-1302 (awq-kernel-opt)

Next week goals:
- Fix KV-cache divergence and land kernel unit test (Ethan + Marco)
- Run full redwood-evals quality sweep (n=2k prompts) for AWQ candidate (Sofia)
- Prepare canary rollout plan and a runbook for rollback (Priya + Jenna)

Appendix (quick raw numbers)
- Baseline float32 cost per 1M tokens: $240(TBD)
- AWQ q4_hybrid est: $173 (28% reduction)
- GPTQ q4 est: $184 (23% reduction)
- NF4 est: $190 (20.8% reduction)
(These are modeled numbers for the sampled workload and will vary by batch distribution.)

Notes to self (Priya):
- Remind infra to snapshot the staging cluster before large sweep runs.
- Schedule a 30-min sync with SRE + Runtime Friday to walk through canary plan.

-----
Raw log (stream-of-consciousness / scratch)
- saw funky tape/stride offset in kernel logs, added printf — weird values at boundary of 16-byte pack. TODO: write a small c-test that simulates padding case and run on all kernels.
- consider adding quant-profile metadata to model catalog: "recommended_deployment_modes": ["dedicated:low-latency","hosted:best-effort"]

End of doc.
